transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SA), Lina Park (Astral CTO), Marcus Holt (Astral Head of ML), Anya Suresh (Astral Platform Eng), Devon Lee (Astral Data Eng)

Auto-generated summary (may be partial): POC scoping for integration plan focusing on SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function calling, structured output; establish success metrics and benchmark plan.

00:00 Jordan Blake: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, can you hear us ok?
00:04 Lina Park: Yep loud and clear thanks Jordan.
00:06 Marcus Holt: All good. We got about 50 minutes, hope that's fine.
00:10 Jordan Blake: Yep great, we've got Priya and Marco with me, we'll run through how Redwood's endpoints fit into Astral's flow, then go into benchmarks and timeline and wrap with next steps.
00:18 Priya Menon: Quick note, I'm going to focus on integration patterns - SDKs, the OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and function/tool calling. Marco will cover performance knobs.
00:29 Marcus Holt: Sounds good. High level for context: our main use case is automated summarization + entity extraction across analyst notes, roughly 250k docs, steady ingestion with bursts. We also want embeddings for semantic search. Key constraints are latency and cost - we have a 99th percentile latency target for UI interactions.
00:44 Jordan Blake: Great - Lina are you able to share the exact success criteria? I think we had an email thread but wanted to confirm live.
00:50 Lina Park: Sure - primary things: P95 latency under 450ms for generation calls at ~512 token average; embedding throughput of ~200 req/s with 128-dim (actually our vector size is 1536) sorry, brain fart - 1536 dims, we mean 200 req/s sustained. Also accuracy/regression: extraction F1 not to drop more than 2 points versus our current baseline.
01:10 Priya Menon: Okay that's helpful. On the Redwood side we'll match those with a benchmark plan: steady-state and burst scenarios, and we'll include cache-warm vs cold runs. We recommend running both Hosted and a small Dedicated pool to compare unit cost.
01:25 Devon Lee: Quick Q - when you say Dedicated pool do you mean reserved GPU nodes or dedicated VPC hosts? We prefer reserved GPUs but want VPC connectivity.
01:32 Marco Ruiz: Good question. Dedicated refers to reserved GPU capacity in our cloud offering - it's possible to pair that with a Private/VPC control plane for network isolation, but for the POC we usually do a Dedicated pool in Redwood's tenant with a VPC peering tunnel; if you need on-prem or fully private control plane that's a different rollout.
01:48 Anya Suresh: For the POC we just need isolation and not to send PII outside, so VPC peering + KMS for keys would be ideal. Do you support customer-managed KMS?
01:55 Priya Menon: Yes, we support integrating with customer KMS/HSM for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we have envelope encryption and SOC2 controls but if you need full KMS you can run Dedicated with customer KMS tied to the VPC.
02:08 Lina Park: Good. Next, SDKs: our engineering prefers JS + Python SDKs; we also use an internal Golang service that might call the endpoint. How compatible are your SDKs with the OpenAI client patterns?
02:17 Jordan Blake: Very compatible - Redwood provides OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints and SDKs that mirror their API surface for chat/completions/embeddings and also support our extended features like structured output and function calling. Priya?
02:26 Priya Menon: Right, the SDKs have small extension points. For example, our function-calling follows OpenAI's tooling where you can declare schema and Redwood returns structured JSON. We also support enforced schema validation on the server side to reduce parsing errors.
02:38 Marcus Holt: So we can swap out calls that currently hit OpenAI with Redwood's URL and use the same client? Any changes needed for auth?
02:45 Marco Ruiz: Typically you change the base URL and the API key header. We also support API keys with scoped roles. If you want OpenAI-compatible tooling ready, we can provide a short script to swap endpoints and run smoke tests.
02:58 Devon Lee: That would make benchmarking easier, yes.
03:02 Priya Menon: We'll include a migration smoke-test in the benchmark plan. Also note that Redwood supports streaming and chunked responses for long generations - important for UI latency.
03:12 Lina Park: On function calling and tools: we plan to call internal enrichment services (entity resolver, taxonomy lookup) and want the model to return a JSON with fields {entities:[], confidence, canonical_text}. Can Redwood enforce that?
03:24 Priya Menon: Yes - you can declare a schema for the structured output and enable strict mode so the model must comply or Redwood returns an error-like payload for broken outputs. We also supply a post-processor validation hook if you want custom checks.
03:38 Marcus Holt: Good. For the extraction F1 we need deterministic-ish outputs; do you provide eval harnesses?
03:44 Marco Ruiz: We do - Redwood Optimize includes evaluation tooling tied to prompt sets and reference labels, so we can run regression tests across model and quantization changes. For the POC we'll run your labeled sample through the harness.
03:56 Lina Park: Walk me through the benchmark metrics again. P95 latency 450ms, embedding throughput 200 req/s, cost below X (we'll share target). Anything else?
04:10 Jordan Blake: We'll measure P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, throughput for embeddings, cold vs warm KV cache, and token cost per 1k tokens. We'll also capture inference error rates and structured-output schema compliance.
04:24 Devon Lee: Regarding KV cache - our typical prompt has a 256 token prefix (context snippets) that repeat a lot. Do you support prefix caching to reduce cost?
04:32 Priya Menon: Yes that's one of the big win areas. Redwood supports prefix/KV caching, and in Dedicated you can tune cache sizes based on sequence distribution. We'll instrument cache hit rates in the benchmark logs.
04:45 Marcus Holt: Network latency matters; can we run the Dedicated pool in a region close to our infra? We're on GCP us-central1.
04:53 Marco Ruiz: Absolutely - we have capacity in us-central and us-west. For Dedicated POC we'll provision nodes in us-central to minimize egress latency.
05:02 Lina Park: Timeline - we need POC results within three weeks to present to execs. Is that feasible?
05:08 Jordan Blake: Yes, typical timeline: 1-2 days to provision test environment, 3 days to run smoke tests and warm caches, 7 days for sustained benchmark (you asked for 1-week), then 2-3 days to analyze and present results. So start on 2027-05-16 and wrap by 2027-05-26 meets your three-week window.
05:26 Priya Menon: We'll also add a mid-run checkpoint at day 3 to adjust batch sizes and quantization parameters.
05:33 Lina Park: Speaking of quantization: we might be open to 8-bit quant to save cost if accuracy holds. Do you support quantized variants and can you auto-route fallback to float when accuracy drops?
05:44 Marco Ruiz: Yes - Redwood supports multiple model variants and smart routing policies. For the POC we'll test an int8 quantized variant and measure F1 delta; we can set automated fallback for a small percentage of traffic if regression exceeds threshold.
05:58 Marcus Holt: Security stuff quickly - SSO, audit logs, SOC2 evidence. We need SAML/SCIM, audit log export and retention options.
06:08 Priya Menon: We support SAML (IdP metadata), SCIM provisioning, and per-request audit logs with configurable retention. For Dedicated and Private you can tune retention and export to your SIEM via Kinesis or Pub/Sub. We'll attach the SOC2 pack to the ticket.
06:22 Anya Suresh: Any blockers around data residency? We need logs to stay in us region.
06:28 Marco Ruiz: You can configure log export endpoints to stay in us, and Dedicated nodes will operate in your chosen region.
06:33 Lina Park: Ok good. Now a few nitty-gritty integration questions: 1) How does function/tool calling work with our internal enrichment services behind a firewall? 2) How to handle retries and idempotency for enrichment calls triggered by model?
06:46 Priya Menon: For internal tools behind firewall we support a webhook proxy inside your VPC - Redwood will call an endpoint in the peered network, or you can run a small relay that fetches tasks. For idempotency we recommend passing dedupe keys from the model output; Redwood's orchestration can set timeouts and a retry policy but the relay should be idempotent. We'll include an example relay in the repo we share.
07:04 Devon Lee: When streaming, do you expose incremental structured chunks or only the final validated payload?
07:10 Priya Menon: Both. You can stream partial tokens for low-latency UI and optionally request final structured payload with schema enforcement at the end. If you enable strict schema, the final validated JSON will be separate event.
07:23 Marcus Holt: For embeddings: do you support batch endpoints and asynchronous processing? We want to embed large ingests overnight.
07:30 Marco Ruiz: Yes - embeddings batch endpoints with up to 1k inputs per request and an async job API for very large jobs. We also have connectors for S3/GCS for bulk ingestion.
07:40 Lina Park: Perfect. Let's confirm success criteria in the call so we have it captured: 1) Gen P95 < 450ms for 512 token average, 2) Embedding throughput 200 req/s sustained, 3) Extraction F1 drop < 2 pts, 4) Budget target TBD but we'll share.
07:56 Jordan Blake: Noted. We'll include those as acceptance tests in the POC.
08:00 Priya Menon: Ok I'll outline the benchmark plan now: phase 0 - environment setup and security checks (2 days), phase 1 - smoke & migration test (3 days), phase 2 - sustained benchmark (7 days), phase 3 - analysis and presentation (2-3 days). We will run Hosted and Dedicated variants and compare cost and latency.
08:19 Lina Park: Do you need any instrumentation from our side? We can provide low-level traces and a synthetic user agent.
08:25 Marco Ruiz: We'll need a traffic profile (QPS, token lengths, percent of streaming vs non-streaming, cacheable prefix rate) and sample prompts with expected labels. Also a small labeled testset for F1 measurement.
08:40 Devon Lee: We'll prepare that, expect it by Tuesday.
08:44 Jordan Blake: Great. On commercials - we'll send a draft SOW and pricing for the Dedicated trial. Anything specific on licensing?
08:52 Lina Park: We'll be evaluating cost per 1M tokens and embedding unit price; try to map to our cloud spend model.
08:59 Jordan Blake: Understood, we'll include those.
09:02 Marcus Holt: One more technical: how do you measure exact tokenization differences between models? We need consistent token counts for cost.
09:10 Priya Menon: We'll use Redwood's tokenizer tool to report token counts per prompt and include it in the benchmark logs. For model variance we'll pin model versions in the POC.
09:20 Lina Park: Sounds good. Any known limitations or gotchas?
09:24 Marco Ruiz: If you use extremely long contexts >8k tokens some kernels ramp differently; we'll note that but your workload is much smaller. Also strict schema enforcement can sometimes require prompt engineering to reach 100% compliance, we'll iterate on prompts in the run.
09:40 Jordan Blake: Ok let's recap and capture next steps.
09:44 Jordan Blake: Next steps: Jordan to send SOW & pricing, Priya to share benchmark scripts and evaluation harness, Marco to provision us-central Dedicated pool and share connection steps, Astral to provide traffic profile and labeled sample. Target start 2027-05-16.
09:58 Lina Park: Yep that's accurate. I'll confirm IdP method and get the sample data by Tuesday.
10:02 Marcus Holt: Thanks everyone, excited to run this.
10:06 Jordan Blake: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the ticket and repo links.

Action items (auto): Jordan to send docs; Priya to share scripts; Lina to send sample traffic profile.

References noted during call: POC benchmark spreadsheet (link shared in chat), SOC2 pack (link), demo repo with relay example (link).

End of transcript.
